_note: Declared caption-tier verdicts for the book's authored figure/table captions. Each key is a caption id: for a figure, the `figure:` asset path (already unique in chapter scope); for a table, `<chapter-file>::<short>` using the table's existing `[short: ...]` print-index name (single source of truth: the same string the list-of-tables uses). `tier` is A|B|C — the caption's argumentative role (A Anchor 4-8 sentences/60-120 words; B Supporting 2-4/25-70; C Reference 1-2/<=30). `kind` and `location` are the classification axes; `rationale` is one line. Mirrors the brick-fitness.json genre: a flat declared map with a _note provenance block, no hardcoded list in the builder or lint. Consumed by book-models/lint_caption_length.py, which measures each authored caption's length against its tier band (A carries a floor: an under-written anchor is a finding). A new figure/table with no row here is itself a finding (drift defense). Source of the first-pass verdicts + the ratified A/B borderline resolutions (constraint-vs-sensor=A, services-reactive-view=A, join-composite=A, llm-as-function-call=B): book/_design/drafts/caption-tier-model-260806.md. The lint lands AUDIT-ONLY (rule #55): the current tree squeezed every caption to <=3 sentences/<=50 words under the retired uniform cap, so all 17 A-tier captions are under-length today; the Phase-3 rewrite wave drains the findings to 0, then the lint promotes to blocking.
